purpose: Two functions. First, it specifies the request and response format that a party ingesting a work under these terms is asked to support in order to satisfy MRT-3. Second, it is the publisher's own endpoint, since the publisher is also an ingesting party in respect of works it reuses.

anonymity.note: A party may not condition production of the provenance record on the requester proving who they are. Rate limiting is permitted, but only by request shape and volume, never by requester identity.

work.description: URL of the work, or its terms_version_reference, or a content hash.

dataset_id.description: Where the requester already knows which corpus is in question.

reply_token.description: An opaque token generated by the requester, at least 128 bits of entropy. The response is retrieved by presenting this token. No return address is collected, which is what allows the exchange to complete without identifying the requester.

retrieval.description: The requester polls this path. The token is the only credential and the responding party does not learn who holds it.

fields.licence_at_collection: The licence in force when the work was collected.
fields.terms_version_reference_at_collection: The version of these terms in force when the work was collected.
fields.dataset_id: Identifier of the corpus the work entered.
fields.responder: The accountable party producing the record.

refusal_codes.not_ingested: The party holds no record of the work in any corpus.
refusal_codes.no_record: The work was ingested but no provenance record was created. This is a failure of MRT-2 and is recorded as such.
refusal_codes.out_of_scope: The request does not identify a work the party publishes or ingests.
refusal_codes.refused: The party declines to answer. A reason is given.

note: A refusal is a valid response and is more useful than silence, because a recorded refusal is attributable. Absence of any response is itself evidence that the party cannot produce the record.
